Cautiously positive, now reinforced by SLOOS and the April 2021 Beige Book. The Beige Book reports modest-to-moderate gains in national activity with consumer spending and tourism improving, and employment strengthening—helped by vaccinations—particularly in manufacturing, construction, and leisure/hospitality. It also notes wage firming amid hiring challenges for low-wage and hourly workers. These developments are broadly consistent with the FOMC’s view that activity and employment have strengthened. On prices, the Beige Book highlights cost increases tied to supply chain disruptions and even weather effects, aligning with the statement’s characterization of largely transitory inflation pressures. Together with SLOOS evidence of easing credit standards across consumer categories and for investment‑grade firms, the credit backdrop looks more supportive of the Fed’s aim to keep the flow of credit to households and businesses. Offsetting factors remain: standards are not uniformly eased, some segments are tighter than pre‑pandemic, and recovery is uneven across borrower types and sectors.

Netting these Beige Book insights with SLOOS, the stance remains constructive with measured risks; we tilt the assessment modestly more positive than before.
